title: Set up a project
summary: During the founding interview, you describe the tool and the agent records its purpose, risks and first pieces of work.

checks.description: The tooling check reports whether required tools and GitHub access are available before building begins.
The agent enables Git’s pre-push hook, which blocks direct pushes to the main branch. An agent can bypass it; only Claude Code settings refuse the --no-verify bypass.
Branch protection requires the project check to pass on GitHub where your GitHub plan allows it.
The first upload requires your approval.
Without a selected recipe, the initial project check deliberately fails until the agent replaces the placeholder with real project tests.
Recipe projects skip the placeholder and use the starter's recipe-check workflow for application checks.

person_decides: You answer the founding interview questions and decide whether to use existing work.

title: Shape a piece
summary: You and the agent agree on one piece and the decisions it needs.

checks.description: The readiness script adds the ready label, meaning the piece is ready to build, only when it has acceptance criteria under Done when, records its risk areas and records decisions for open-question labels such as needs-answers. Projects with code also require a Reaches line, which lists the code areas the piece may change.
The reach check identifies the files the piece may affect.
The agent gives a risk notice for work touching a risk area whose caution has not been completed and whose risk has not been accepted, and records your decision and the date.

person_decides: You settle questions that need your judgement, then decide whether to run /implement on the ready piece.

title: Implement a piece
summary: The agent builds one ready piece, then scripts and a reviewer agent assess the change.

checks.description: The test protection check rejects unexplained edits to tests frozen by a commit whose subject starts with Test:. Changes to existing test lines need a Test fix: commit with a reason; a later Test: commit may add lines.

The test evidence check reports when tests passed before the change was made or acceptance criteria have no matching tests. Criteria marked for you to try are excluded from the automated test mapping.

The structure script reports new circular dependencies, where parts of the code depend on each other in a loop. The agent checks boundary crossings with a project tool, if available, or by examining changed dependencies.
The clean-up script refuses to save a clean-up that changes tests or their supporting files.
In Claude Code, secret protection hooks block commands that match their secret-detection rules.
The repair reset script removes a failed repair before the next attempt, so failed fixes do not accumulate.

person_decides: By default, you try the result and decide whether to merge the named pull request. Automatic merging requires your explicit decision and recorded limits.

title: Review the change
summary: A reviewer agent assesses the change and its evidence in a separate session.

checks.description: The review packet contains the change and supporting evidence. The review record identifies the version reviewed.
The review protection script restores changed or deleted files that it copied before the review; it reports other changes without restoring them.
The review check fails the project check while a finding marked worth stopping for remains unresolved or the review record identifies a different version.

person_decides: You decide which findings the agent fixes. You can ask it to explain a finding first.

title: Merge the change
summary: By default, the merge script verifies your recorded approval for the named change and the project check results before merging.

checks.description: The merge script requires your recorded approval unless you have enabled automatic merging. It merges only the version that was checked.
The risk-area check reports the areas affected by the change and blocks merging while a risk decision remains unresolved.

For a live project, the settings script identifies new setting names in .env.example, the example file listing the project’s required settings. The agent waits for hosting setup to confirm them before requesting a merge.

person_decides: By default, you tell the agent in conversation to merge the named pull request, and it records your words and the date. Automatic merging requires your explicit decision and recorded limits.

title: Set up or check the live tool
summary: On a recipe, the launch script blocks recording a live address until the backup and way back are confirmed.

checks.description: On a recipe, the launch script blocks recording a live address if no backup is confirmed or no way back is defined. It cannot stop a host that deploys on merge. With no recipe, it gives a one-time notice that recipe checks cannot run.
Before a live change, the approval script verifies that an unused approval names that exact change.
The live check compares the live version with the main branch on Vercel or Coolify without changing the live copy.
The live check compares the live version with the main branch without changing the live copy.

person_decides: You decide whether to launch after the agent explains the proposed live change.

title: Maintain the project
summary: The agent checks project records and the live copy (the running tool on its host), then runs monthly or quarterly upkeep when due.

checks.description: The live check runs at every maintenance visit.
The update check lists the follow-up work that maintenance needs to complete after a kit update.
The recipe freshness check reports recipes missing from the current menu, recipes last checked more than 90 days ago, and superseded settings still used by the project.
The branch report lists branches whose work has already been merged into the main branch. It deletes nothing.
The instruction length check reports when the standing instructions reach 200 lines.
The Claude Code settings script offers updated safety rules and applies them only with your approval.

person_decides: You decide whether to apply changes beyond routine updates.
